content:
maria: quick sync — after last night's billing drift incident, we need a short design check-in on tenant-stitching fallback patterns when billing key / tenant id is missing. CC: @aj @chloe @samir. Want to settle on: a) fields we emit b) pre-enrich vs late-bind c) how to surface confidence/cost tradeoffs.

aj: +1. I think the core ask: when envelope lacks billing_key, we can 1) try header-based stitching (edge proxy), 2) lookup via session_id, 3) finally fallback to fingerprinting. Each step should attach a `stitch_source` and `stitch_confidence`.

chloe: agree. Also: avoid PII -> no raw IPs in logs. If we fingerprint, emit only hash and mark as ephemeral. And mark these traces as non-deterministic for billing queries.

samir: big flag: sampling. If we do fingerprinting or late-lookup, it's expensive. Need to cap the number of late-enrich attempts per minute per tenant. For the incident we saw 2k lookups/min from a single service.

aj: proposal sketch:
```
// envelope attrs
billing_key: optional
stitch_hint: ["edge_header","session_id","fingerprint"]
stitch_source: "edge_header"
stitch_confidence: "high" | "medium" | "low"
```
On missing billing_key, edge sets `stitch_hint` when it has something.

maria: +1 on fields. Also we need `billing_key_resolution`: "pre-enriched" | "late_enriched" | "unresolved". This helps cost dashboards to attribute unknowns.

kevin: about storage: unresolved traces should not be expensive. Suggest TTL 7d and cheaper indexing. Also we should tag unresolved for separate aggregation pipeline so they don't inflate tenant costs.

chloe: security: any late enrich that uses customer-owned tenant lookup (call to tenant mapping service) must be rate-limited and audited. We should add `lookup_path` metadata: e.g., `lookup_path: "svc-tenant-lookup-v2"`. That helps debug.

samir: edge-case: what if the lookup returns multiple candidates? We should emit `candidates_count` and prefer conservative choice (don't attribute) if ambiguity >1.

aj: fallback policy: attempt in-order: edge header -> session_id lookup -> tenant mapping -> fingerprint. Stop when confidence >= medium. If none, set `billing_key_resolution=unresolved` and `stitch_confidence=low`.

maria: opt-in rollout: enable fingerprint fallback only for <5% of traffic initially with canary flag and observe false positives. Also expose metrics: `stitch_attempts_total`, `stitch_success_by_source`, `stitch_unresolved_total`.

kevin: metric labels: source, service, env. Keep cardinality low.

chloe: comment: for queries that need exact billing (billing pipeline), unresolved should be forwarded to delayed reconciliation job that tries heavier heuristics once per hour.

samir: correct. Also add budget guard: if late-lookup rate spikes, circuit-break whole late-enrich path and fall back to `unresolved` with an incident alert.

maria: agree. Action items:
- aj: RFC PR for envelope fields + sample event examples (due EOD Wed)
- chloe: security review checklist for late-lookup (due Fri)
- kevin: cheaper index TTL plan + metric labels (due Thu)
- samir: circuit-break thresholds and canary plan (due Thu)

infra-bot: deploy-log: canary flag toggle `stitch-fingerprint-enabled=false` applied to prod at 2023-11-02T03:12Z :white_check_mark:

aj: thanks all. I'll spin up the draft and ping for quick review. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks. if anyone sees a regression in the next deploy, ping here and we'll escalate.

kevin: one tiny note — add `billing_key_source` enum to include `customer_provided`, `redwood_lookup`, `fingerprint`, `none`.

aj: ok added to RFC list.

chloe: :raised_hands: good plan.
